text:
maria: Noticing persistent 95p latency blasts in eu-west-3 during heavy prefix-warmup windows this morning. Patterns look like intermittent NVLink retransmits + PCIe short stalls, egress proxy queuing spikes.

alex: I see it too. Topology map points to a small set of nodes in rack-12 where GPU p95 jumps and egress_queue_length doubles. Seems correlated with large prefix-generation workloads that refresh KV caches.

jamal: Is this coming from dedicated pools or shared? Any tenant IDs repeating?

maria: Mostly shared. A handful of customers spike roughly at the same hour; not a single noisy tenant, more like many medium jobs aligning.

kevin: I grabbed a short trace (req=tx-wwarm-331): queuing at egress proxy adds ~120ms for some requests, and kernel logs show occasional pci_link_down/recovery messages.

olga: PromQLs? Would like to reproduce the graph.

kevin: Two I used:  
max_over_time(egress_proxy_queue_len{region="eu-west-3"}[10m]) by (node)
and
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le,node))

alex: Hypothesis: warm-kv regen increases intra-node PCIe/NVLink traffic and the egress proxies see bursty backpressure. Multi-resource coupling causes tail.

maria: Quick mitigation idea: carve out tiny warmup silos (2 GPUs) and steer detected warmup traffic there. Give the silo an egress soft-cap so it can't overwhelm shared egress. Call it "warmup-silo".

jamal: How do we detect warmup traffic? We could rely on caller flag, or implement an automated detector: KV-miss-rate delta > 30% over 30s AND request_prefix_length > 128 bytes. Proxy would tag requests with header X-Warmup:1.

olga: Auto-detect seems nice but risky. For immediate rollout use caller-side header, then add detector rule in proxy as follow-up.

alex: Implementation sketch: 1) add node label gpu_silo=warmup to 3 nodes in region; 2) allocation class "warmup-silo-ephemeral" with TTL 8m; 3) proxy route with qos weight 0.25 and token-bucket shaping on egress. Example proxy snippet:  
route: when header("X-Warmup") == "1" -> pool:warmup-slice; pool.qos.weight=0.25; pool.egress.token_rate=50KBps

kevin: Also add a NIC qdisc fallback on node: tc qdisc netem rate-limit to protect uplink if proxy can't keep up.

jamal: I'll create the allocation class in staging:  
apiVersion: v1
kind: AllocationClass
metadata:
  name: warmup-silo-ephemeral
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      gpu_silo: warmup
  ephemeralTTL: 8m
  preemptible: false

kevin: I can run a traffic replay that mimics the warmup-kv regen (burst of prefix-gen requests + high kv-miss) against staging-eu3-warmup (3 nodes).

olga: SRE-bot: create test-only alert warmup-silo-pressure with 3m hold, slack-only.

sre-bot: Created alert warmup-silo-pressure (severity: warning), paging disabled.

kevin: Replay results (staging): compared to shared baseline, warmup-silo reduced egress p95 by ~52% and NVLink retransmit counter dropped ~58%. Median latency unchanged. Token throughput down ~4% on the warmup path due to shaping.

maria: Sounds promising. What's the cost delta?

kevin: Estimated infra delta ~+1.7% regionally because isolating warmups requires reserved mini-silos. But customer-visible latency improvements are material for many tenants.

alex: Rollout plan proposal: canary at 5% warmup traffic for 30m, monitor metrics and these rollback gates: 1) region_egress_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5; 2) nvlink_err_rate > baseline * 2; 3) warmup-silo-egress_queue_len > 100 for >2m. If any trigger fires, flip traffic back to shared.

jamal: Ops changes: add label gpu_silo=warmup to two underutilized racks in eu-west-3, create allocation class, and add route in proxy config. Then enable caller header at SDK level for warmup triggers.

olga: I'll open a finance ticket to set a cost cap for the canary and mark the mini-silo nodes to neutral billing for the trial.

kevin: Small request: add per-slice egress_p95 and per-route token_rate metrics to the console so product can see customer impact.

maria: Good call. Also add an opt-out mechanism: a tenant flag to opt-out of warmup silo during the trial if they prefer no egress shaping.

alex: Final runbook snippet for oncall if things go wrong: 1) disable warmup route in proxy; 2) scale down allocation class to 0; 3) revert SDK header rollout; 4) escalate to infra with nvlink logs and last-good time.

jamal: Staging allocation and labels created, replay run uploaded to perf-jobs, results attached in drive.

maria: Moving to canary per plan. I'll post a short note to #product and #support so they know about possible transient changes during the 5% canary.

olga: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: we'll implement the in-proxy detector in phase 2 and run another set of tests before global roll.
